architecture.title: Stage 1 at a glance
architecture.alt: C source flows through the Trace Engine, schema-2 JSON, TraceStore, then validated semantic evidence; Stage 2 consumes the qualified results.
architecture.caption: The parser does not execute C; the future Semantic Engine does not change what the recorder observed.

compilation.title: Compilation to observation
compilation.alt: Build config enters GCC; the debug binary is run under GDB with a linked allocation wrapper; a separate sanitized binary is available for a later diagnostic run.

checkpoint.title: GDB command and checkpoint lifecycle
checkpoint.alt: At a stopped PC the engine drains events and observes memory, then sends a tokened MI instruction step and awaits an asynchronous stop before recording an outcome.

nodes.label: Observed *stopped
lines: Stop ID, frame PC = next instruction

nodes.label: Drain telemetry · checkpoint
lines: Read stack and memory only while stopped

nodes.label: Wait for next *stopped
lines: Timeout, signal and exit handled separately

nodes.label: Retain event or gap
lines: Before PC, outcome, next PC if observed

stack.title: Frames and variable observations
stack.alt: A stop contains a frame-zero variable vector, optional bounded caller frame vectors, a separate global vector, and separately budgeted raw bytes.

heap.title: Heap lifetime, reuse and realloc
heap.alt: Malloc starts ID 1. Free ends ID 1. A later allocation at the same address receives ID 2. Successful realloc can create a linked new ID, but only event and lifetime evidence verifies the link.

nodes.label: malloc(A) → ID 1
lines: PID-local event sequence; first lifetime begins

nodes.label: free(A) → end ID 1
lines: Historical bytes never become live again

nodes.label: malloc(A) → ID 2
lines: Same numeric address, new identity; old pointer origin unknown

nodes.label: realloc(ID 2) → ID 3
lines: Only corroborated event + lifetime link is definite

metadata.title: Static metadata versus observed runtime
metadata.alt: GCC DWARF describes compiled types and declarations; optional Clang AST describes syntax; GDB observes stopped runtime; fusion only records bounded candidate links.

records.title: DebugSessionTrace relationships
records.alt: A top-level trace contains snapshots, disassembly and instruction events, gaps and source checkpoints, heap records and lifetimes, and independent tool reports.

ownership.title: One trace, many borrowed readers
ownership.alt: TraceStore holds an Arc of the canonical trace and an Arc of position indexes; borrowed views and trace-scoped EvidenceRef resolve to those original records.

confidence.title: Validation and confidence are different gates
confidence.alt: Deserialization checks schema; opt-in deep validation detects structural corruption or partial/unavailable evidence; confidence qualifies each relationship; Stage 2 interprets without inventing observations.

consumer.title: TP-6 and TP-7 consumer path
consumer.alt: A single validated view holds the report and borrows the store; checkpoint summary and bounded pages provide trace-scoped references and qualified events without copying records.

partial.title: From failure to qualified partial evidence
partial.alt: GDB timeout, trace-byte cap or missing child ACK keeps whatever records were safely observed; coverage and stage status mark the missing scope; the parser reports partial or unavailable, not fabricated success.

nodes.label: Retain observed prefix
lines: Snapshots, events and diagnostics if available

nodes.label: Validate and downgrade
lines: Partial ≠ structural corruption; links may be unavailable

handoff.title: Stage 1 → Stage 2 boundary
handoff.alt: Stage 1 gives a validated borrowed evidence view; Stage 2 may compose explanations but must preserve observation scope and uncertainty, without claiming pointer provenance or AST execution.
